label: digit 1 at position 1-2 right after one of {h,3,b,z,2,u} at sequence start
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, only when the input token is the digit 1, and only at t=1 (85% of mass) or t=2. At t=1 it fires exactly when the first token is one of h, 3, b, z, 2, u (precision 1.0 for that clause). Magnitude depends on that first token: b is highest (about 1.0 of max), then z and 3 (about 0.8), h (about 0.74), and u and 2 are lowest (about 0.26). At t=2 it fires more weakly, mostly when both earlier tokens are in the set (e.g. h 3 1), and sometimes when only the immediately preceding token is (g h 1, g b 1). Never fires on 1 after other tokens, at later positions, or in the delimiter/copy phases.

issues: The t=1 part checks out. in_tok=1, t=1 and prev_tok in {h,3,b,z,2,u} has precision 1.0 and recall 0.81 on its own. Firing is limited to the original phase at t=1 and t=2 (85% and 15% of activation mass). There is no activation in the delimiter or copy phases and none on other input tokens.

The t=2 rule is wrong in a systematic way. The original predicate requires the first token to be in {h,3,b,z,2,u}, but the test misses (318 steps, 6.4% of mass) include many t=2 hits with first tokens e, f and j: e z 1, f b 1, j z 1, j 3 1, j h 1, j b 1. The explanation calls these 'sometimes when only the token just before is', but they form a whole class.

There are systematic false positives at t=2 (235 on test), mostly where the earlier tokens are 2 or u (2 3 1, b 2 1, 2 u 1, 3 u 1, u u 1). The real t=2 rule is that prev_tok is in {h,3,b,z} (not 2 or u) and first_tok is in {b,e,f,g,h,j,u,z,3}. Splitting dev by first token gives precision of exactly 1.0 or 0.0 for each value. prev_tok=u at t=2 has precision 0.0 and prev_tok=2 has 0.44.
Because of these errors, coverage in the second activation quartile is only 0.71: the weaker t=2 activations are badly captured.
The label overclaims. It says the feature needs the first token to be in the set at t=2, which is false. It also treats 2 and u as valid previous tokens at t=2, but those almost never fire there.
skeptic.revised_label: digit 1 at t=1 right after one of {h,3,b,z,2,u}; or digit 1 at t=2 right after one of {h,3,b,z} when the first token is one of {b,e,f,g,h,j,u,z,3}
